entities.name: PMID:25098018
observations: 2014 experiment enrolled 56 university students classified as introverts or extroverts with the Eysenck Personality Questionnaire.
Participants performed a sequential-timing keyboard task under self-controlled or yoked/external feedback conditions, with practice, retention, and transfer phases.

entities.name: Self-controlled feedback benefit
observations: Self-controlled feedback improved motor learning relative to yoked feedback: F(1,52)=4.13, p<.05, eta-squared=.07.
The reported benefit occurred regardless of personality trait; no introversion-by-feedback differential enhancement was reported.

entities.name: Personality evidence limitation
observations: The accessible abstract does not report phase-specific introvert/extrovert means, interaction tests, or separate retention and transfer effects.
No additional direct experimental study was identified in targeted searches; replication with continuous personality scores and powered interaction tests is needed.
